Build a signed systemd-boot A/B release with a verified root from an existing
root filesystem.

## Inputs

| Name                 | Kind      | Default       | Description                                                                                                                                    |
| -------------------- | --------- | ------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `kernel`             | file      | **Required**  | Target Linux kernel image.                                                                                                                     |
| `initrd`             | file      | **Required**  | Initrd implementing the core verified-root boot contract.                                                                                      |
| `rootfs`             | directory | **Required**  | Prepared root filesystem implementing the core verified-root boot contract.                                                                    |
| `boot-certificate`   | file      | **Required**  | PEM-encoded RSA X.509 certificate for signing EFI boot artifacts.                                                                              |
| `bundle-certificate` | file      | **Required**  | Single PEM-encoded X.509 end-entity signer certificate issued directly by the trusted root. No intermediates. The default signer requires RSA. |
| `secure-boot-keys`   | directory | `{"tree":{}}` | Authenticated variables PK.auth, KEK.auth, and db.auth that systemd-boot enrolls in Setup Mode. Empty by default, disabling enrollment.        |

## Parameters

| Name               | Default      | Description                                                                                                             |
| ------------------ | ------------ | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `architecture`     | **Required** | Target architecture: amd64 or arm64. Must match the system architecture.                                                |
| `cmdline-extra`    | `""`         | Additional authenticated kernel arguments.                                                                              |
| `panic-timeout`    | `10`         | Kernel panic reboot delay in seconds. Zero leaves the system stopped.                                                   |
| `boot-timeout`     | `0`          | systemd-boot menu timeout in seconds.                                                                                   |
| `signing-time`     | `""`         | Signing time as Unix seconds in a string. Empty uses the build source epoch.                                            |
| `config-size`      | `0`          | ESP capacity in bytes. Zero reserves three copies of its current files, uses at least 256 MiB, and rounds up to 64 MiB. |
| `root-compression` | `"none"`     | SquashFS compression of the root filesystem, such as zstd or xz, or none.                                               |
| `disk-size`        | `0`          | Factory disk capacity in bytes. Zero sizes the disk from its partitions.                                                |
| `secondary-config` | `false`      | Reserve an empty secondary configuration partition with the same capacity as the ESP.                                   |

## Rule Parameters

Callers can replace these operations through `rules` bindings. An implementation
receives the listed inputs and parameters and must produce the listed outputs.
See [Rule Parameters](/docs/bakery/next/build-rules#rule-parameters).

### `efi-signer`

Sign an EFI executable. Bakery verifies each signature against boot-certificate.

Default implementation: `core/sign-efi`.

| Name           | Role      | Kind | Description                                                                   |
| -------------- | --------- | ---- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `image`        | Input     | file | Unsigned PE executable: the UKI or systemd-boot.                              |
| `certificate`  | Input     | file | The boot-certificate input.                                                   |
| `signing-time` | Parameter |      | Signing time as Unix seconds in a string. Empty means the build source epoch. |
| `image`        | Output    | file | PE executable with a UEFI Secure Boot signature.                              |

### `bundle-signer`

Create a CMS signature over the bundle's signed metadata. Bakery verifies it
against bundle-certificate.

Default implementation: `core/sign-cms`.

| Name           | Role      | Kind | Description                                                                      |
| -------------- | --------- | ---- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `content`      | Input     | file | Signed bundle metadata.                                                          |
| `certificate`  | Input     | file | The bundle-certificate input.                                                    |
| `signing-time` | Parameter |      | Signing time as Unix seconds in a string. Empty means the build source epoch.    |
| `signature`    | Output    | file | DER-encoded CMS SignedData with the encapsulated content and signer certificate. |

## Execution

Composes other rules into a build graph.

## Behavior

Build an EFI A/B release with a verified root from an existing root filesystem,
kernel, and initrd. The composition builds a SquashFS root filesystem, appends
dm-verity authentication data, embeds the root hash and image geometry in a
Unified Kernel Image (UKI), signs and verifies the UKI and systemd-boot, and
assembles a factory GPT disk and signed Rugix update bundle.

The required `architecture` is `amd64` or `arm64` and must match the kernel. The
root filesystem supplies `etc/os-release`. The initrd must implement the
[core verified-root boot contract](../../recipes/debian-verified-root/); custom
distributions can implement the same contract independently.

The factory disk contains the EFI System Partition (ESP) with the initial
`rugix-a.efi` UKI and the A system partition with the combined root image. The
ESP also carries the bootstrap marker and becomes Rugix Ctrl's configuration
partition at `/run/rugix/mounts/config`. On first boot, Rugix Ctrl preserves the
ESP, expands the system capacity, creates an empty B system partition, and
creates data in the remaining drive space according to the root filesystem's
bootstrap plan. The platform setup recipe defaults both system slots to at least
4 GiB. [The EFI layout rule](../layout-efi-ab/) describes the factory and
completed layouts.

Factory sizing requires no size settings:

- Root: SquashFS sized to its contents, followed by verity data.
- ESP: reserve three copies of the current boot files, use at least 256 MiB, and
  round up to 64 MiB.
- Disk: fit the factory partition layout automatically.

`root-compression` selects the SquashFS compression of the root filesystem and
defaults to `none`, which helps delta updates find unchanged data. Select a
compressor such as `zstd` or `xz` for smaller images.

`config-size` and `disk-size` are optional factory capacity overrides. The
bootstrap plan controls deployed system capacities and data allocation. Once
bootstrapped, future payloads must fit the deployed slots. `signing-time` is
Unix seconds encoded as a string; empty uses the build source epoch.

The bundle delivers combined `system.img` and signed `boot.efi` payloads to
Rugix Ctrl slots named `system` and `boot`. The consuming root filesystem must
configure those slots as corresponding A/B boot groups.

| Output        | Contents                                                            |
| ------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `image`       | Factory disk                                                        |
| `bundle`      | Signed update bundle                                                |
| `uki`         | Signed UKI                                                          |
| `bootloader`  | Signed systemd-boot executable                                      |
| `root-hash`   | Root hash embedded in the UKI                                       |
| `hash-offset` | Byte offset of the appended hash area, as decimal text              |
| `data-size`   | SquashFS length in bytes before padding and hashes, as decimal text |

The firmware must trust `boot-certificate` and enforce Secure Boot. Configure
the firmware separately, or let the factory image enroll your keys as described
in [Enroll Secure Boot Keys](#enroll-secure-boot-keys).

Supply one PEM-encoded certificate as `bundle-certificate`; the default bundle
signer requires RSA. The bundle embeds only this signer certificate, without
intermediates. Issue it directly from the root that Rugix Ctrl trusts. The
signer must not be a CA certificate.

## Signers

Two rule parameters sign the release:

- `efi-signer` signs the UKI and systemd-boot. It defaults to
  [`core/sign-efi`](../sign-efi/), which uses a private key file.
- `bundle-signer` signs the update bundle's metadata. It defaults to
  [`core/sign-cms`](../sign-cms/), which uses a private key file.

Bind the private keys of the default signers through `rules`:

```toml
rules.efi-signer.secrets.key = { path = "keys/boot.key" }
rules.bundle-signer.secrets.key = { path = "keys/bundle.key" }
```

To keep private keys in an HSM or a KMS, bind your own rules instead. A
replacement receives the same inputs and parameters as the default, listed under
Rule Parameters, and may require additional inputs, parameters, and secrets,
which its binding supplies. It may run in its own environment.

```toml
[rules.efi-signer]
uses = "kms-sign-efi"
parameters.key-uri = "pkcs11:token=release;object=boot"
secrets.credentials = { path = "keys/kms-credentials" }
```

Bakery verifies every signature independently of the signer:
[`core/verify-efi`](../verify-efi/) checks EFI signatures against
`boot-certificate`, and
[`core/attach-bundle-signature`](../attach-bundle-signature/) checks the bundle
signature against `bundle-certificate`.

## Customize Boot Settings

Set `cmdline-extra` to supply kernel arguments, such as consoles and log levels.
It defaults to an empty string. The `panic-timeout` parameter defaults to 10
seconds; zero disables automatic reboot after a panic. Verified-root arguments
remain supplied by the composition.

Set `boot-timeout` to control the systemd-boot menu timeout in seconds. For
example:

```toml
parameters.cmdline-extra = "console=ttyS0,115200n8 loglevel=4"
parameters.panic-timeout = 30
parameters.boot-timeout = 5
```

## Enroll Secure Boot Keys

UEFI firmware without a platform key (PK) runs in Setup Mode. It then starts
unsigned boot software and accepts changes to its key databases without
authorization. A factory image can use this state to enroll your keys on its
first boot. Supply the keys as the `secure-boot-keys` directory:

```toml
inputs.secure-boot-keys = { path = "keys/secure-boot" }
```

The directory must contain exactly `PK.auth`, `KEK.auth`, and `db.auth`, signed
updates of the UEFI variables holding the platform key, the key exchange keys
(KEK), and the allowed signature database (db). The db must include
`boot-certificate`, otherwise the firmware rejects the release's boot software
once it enforces Secure Boot. The files hold only certificates and signatures,
so the PK and KEK private keys stay outside the build.

The composition places the files in the ESP at `loader/keys/auto/` and enables
automatic enrollment in systemd-boot's loader configuration. When the firmware
is in Setup Mode, systemd-boot writes db, KEK, and PK, then restarts the device.
Writing PK ends Setup Mode, so the firmware verifies signatures from the next
boot on. The operating system therefore starts only after enrollment. TPM
policies bound to PCR 7, the register in which the firmware records its Secure
Boot state, see the final keys from the first operating system boot on. Outside
Setup Mode, systemd-boot leaves the keys untouched. Updates do not remove them
from the ESP, so a device enrolls them again whenever its firmware returns to
Setup Mode, for example after a reset of its keys.

In a virtual machine, systemd-boot enrolls the keys immediately. On other
machines, it first counts down 15 seconds; pressing a key cancels the
enrollment. Once Secure Boot is enforced, the firmware starts only software that
your db authorizes. This includes option ROMs, the firmware of expansion cards
such as graphics or network cards. Include the certificates of the option ROMs a
device needs, or the device can fail to start them.

For example, create the files with OpenSSL and sbsigntool from the certificates
and private keys `keys/PK.crt`, `keys/PK.key`, `keys/KEK.crt`, `keys/KEK.key`,
and the boot certificate `keys/boot.crt`. PK signs the updates of PK and KEK,
and KEK signs the update of db:

```sh
mkdir keys/secure-boot
owner=$(uuidgen)
attributes=NON_VOLATILE,RUNTIME_ACCESS,BOOTSERVICE_ACCESS,TIME_BASED_AUTHENTICATED_WRITE_ACCESS
for name in PK KEK boot; do
    openssl x509 -in "keys/$name.crt" -outform DER -out "keys/$name.cer"
    sbsiglist --owner "$owner" --type x509 --output "keys/$name.esl" "keys/$name.cer"
done
sbvarsign --attr "$attributes" --key keys/PK.key --cert keys/PK.crt \
    --output keys/secure-boot/PK.auth PK keys/PK.esl
sbvarsign --attr "$attributes" --key keys/PK.key --cert keys/PK.crt \
    --output keys/secure-boot/KEK.auth KEK keys/KEK.esl
sbvarsign --attr "$attributes" --key keys/KEK.key --cert keys/KEK.crt \
    --output keys/secure-boot/db.auth db keys/boot.esl
```

The owner GUID records who added each entry. To keep further certificates in db,
such as the vendor certificate of an option ROM, concatenate their lists with
`keys/boot.esl` before signing.

## Example

For example, assemble prepared artifacts:

```toml
uses = "core/image-efi-verified"
inputs.rootfs = { path = "prepared-root" }
inputs.kernel = { path = "kernel" }
inputs.initrd = { path = "initrd" }
inputs.boot-certificate = { path = "keys/boot.crt" }
inputs.bundle-certificate = { path = "keys/bundle.crt" }
rules.efi-signer.secrets.key = { path = "keys/boot.key" }
rules.bundle-signer.secrets.key = { path = "keys/bundle.key" }
parameters.architecture = "amd64"
```

Save the invocation as `build-rule.toml` and run
`./run-bakery bake rule build-rule.toml build/result`. For Debian roots,
[the Debian wrapper](../image-debian-efi-verified/) also selects a kernel and
generates its initrd.

## Secondary Configuration Partition

To reserve space for a replacement ESP, including systemd-boot, set
`parameters.secondary-config = true`. This adds an empty `config-secondary`
partition with the same capacity as `config`. Both config partitions precede the
system partitions, so `system-a`, `system-b`, and `data` use partition numbers
3, 4, and 5 after bootstrap.

Enable the matching recipe option in the root filesystem's layer:

```toml
[parameters."core/debian-efi-verified-setup"]
secondary_config = true
```

Use this option when provisioning a matching factory layout. Existing
installations need a separate partition-layout migration before receiving the
changed root configuration.

Custom roots must provide equivalent system and bootstrap configurations. The
[EFI layout rule](../layout-efi-ab/) describes the reserved partition. The
update bundle continues to update the root and UKI slots; updating and
activating a replacement ESP requires a separate operation.
